- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.5) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.25), model often underestimates; adjust upward by 1–3% if price is trending up.
- Model consistently overreacts to short-term spikes; cap forecast peak at 2–3% below true peak if sentiment is neutral or negative.
- If true price rises >5% from prior period, model often lags by 1–2 periods; shift forecast up by 1–2 steps in the next 3–5 days.
- Mean reversion bias: if model forecast is >10% above recent 5-day average, reduce by 1–2% per day until convergence.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to underestimate late-period price (last 7–10 days); add 1–2% to final 5–7 days if sentiment is positive.
- If sentiment turns positive after a negative streak, model often misses the momentum; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast starting from day 10 onward.
